# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Three ClusterMAX reports leave only CoreWeave platinum for AI cluster operations.**

**What You Need to Know:** SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX 3.0 leaves CoreWeave the only provider rated platinum across three editions. Dylan Patel, founder of SemiAnalysis, called CoreWeave the operational benchmark for the industry. The rating is an operations score for GPU cloud clusters, not a new chip shipment.

### Top Story
CoreWeave said SemiAnalysis published ClusterMAX 3.0 and that CoreWeave is the only provider rated Platinum in all three editions. Dylan Patel, founder of SemiAnalysis, is quoted by CoreWeave: "CoreWeave remains the operational benchmark for the industry." CoreWeave posted that line on September 23, 2026, with the rating presented as an operations benchmark for the industry, not as a parts launch. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/CoreWeave/status/2102874377284890921)

### Silicon
**CXMT gains ground in DRAM as Samsung and SK Hynix shift capacity to HBM: Digitimes**
Digitimes reports CXMT is gaining ground in DRAM. The same report ties that shift to Samsung and SK Hynix moving more capacity toward HBM. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260924VL219/dram-cxmt-samsung-hbm-capacity.html)

**Aetina launches industrial MXM on the NVIDIA Blackwell platform: Astute Group**
Aetina has launched an industrial MXM module powered by the NVIDIA Blackwell platform. Astute Group reports the module is aimed at autonomous mobile robots, manufacturing, and medical AI. Source: [astutegroup.com](https://www.astutegroup.com/news/general/aetina-launches-industrial-mxm-powered-by-nvidia-blackwell-platform-empowering-amr-manufacturing-and-medical-ai/)

**AMD ties agentic CPU design to thread density and single-core performance: AMD**
AMD CTO Mark Papermaster and Mike Clark, senior vice president, corporate fellow, and chief architect of AMD CPUs, discussed CPU requirements for agentic AI. AMD said the design target is both thread density and strong single-core performance. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/AMD/status/2102860275003035789)

**Supermicro and Arm discuss systems with Arm AGI CPUs: Arm**
At Innovate! EMEA 2026, Trent Prestegar, product marketing manager at Supermicro, and Dilip Ramachandran, senior director of marketing at Arm, discussed solutions featuring Arm AGI CPUs. Supermicro described those systems as built for agentic AI workloads that need performance, efficiency, and scale. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Arm/status/2102848555136496049)

**A network-on-chip for multi-die devices: Semiconductor Engineering**
Semiconductor Engineering describes a network-on-chip that carries native packetized traffic directly across die boundaries. The interface is described as stable and invariant, so the packet format does not have to be rewritten at the die edge. Source: [semiengineering.com](https://semiengineering.com/a-network-on-chip-noc-for-multi-die-devices/)

### Data Centres & Power
**800 VDC architecture for AI infrastructure: Data Center Dynamics**
Data Center Dynamics is carrying a whitepaper on what a shift to 800 VDC means for AI data-centre efficiency, resilience, energy storage, and power distribution. The piece is a power-architecture discussion, not a named campus. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/whitepapers/800-vdc-architecture-for-ai-infrastructure/)

**Huawei unveils UnifiedBus for SuperPoDs and clusters: Data Center Dynamics**
Huawei has released a computing architecture that uses UnifiedBus for cluster and SuperPoD interconnect. Data Center Dynamics, in sponsored product news, says the architecture is meant to address booming compute demand. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/product-news/huawei-unveils-new-unifiedbus-computing-architecture-for-superpods-and-clusters/)

**Nvidia on wasted power in an AI data centre: Techzine Global**
Techzine Global reports that Nvidia says an AI data centre wastes a third of its power. The item is a power-use claim, not a site announcement. Source: [techzine.eu](https://www.techzine.eu/blogs/infrastructure/144511/nvidia-ai-data-center-wastes-a-third-of-its-power/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Qualcomm sticks with TSMC for both 2nm Snapdragon flagships: Digitimes**
Digitimes reports Qualcomm is staying with TSMC for both 2nm Snapdragon flagships. The same report says Samsung is stepping up its foundry push. Source: [digitimes.com](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260924VL210/qualcomm-tsmc-snapdragon-samsung-2nm.html)

**Intel Malaysia expands advanced packaging in Penang: Global Sources**
Global Sources reports Intel Malaysia is expanding advanced packaging capabilities in Penang for AI chips. Source: [globalsources.com](https://www.globalsources.com/sourcing-digest/intel-malaysia-expands-advanced-packaging-capabilities-in-penang-for-ai-chips/?source)

**IC-Link by imec and TSMC expand design access: New Electronics**
New Electronics reports that IC-Link by imec and TSMC are expanding a partnership to improve access to advanced chip design. Source: [newelectronics.co.uk](https://www.newelectronics.co.uk/content/news/ic-link-by-imec-and-tsmc-expand-partnership-improving-access-to-advanced-chip-design)

**Indian silicon startups seek capital past seed: EE Times**
EE Times reports from SEMICON India 2026 that Indian semiconductor startups are seeking capital beyond seed rounds. The pressure point is the step from prototypes and tape-out toward volume production. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/semicon-india-2026-startup-mitra-sheds-light-on-early-stage-silicon-startup-funding/)

### The Teardown: One Laser, Many Wavelengths
Wavelength-division multiplexing puts several colours of light on one fibre so a data-centre link carries more traffic without another strand. The conventional build gives each colour its own laser, plus a driver and a control loop. Channel count and component count move together. Add a colour and you add another laser to power, tune, and watch fail.

An optical frequency comb breaks that pairing. One source produces many evenly spaced wavelengths. On a spectrum analyzer those lines look like the teeth of a comb. Data Center Knowledge reports that AI data centres are scaling toward 16 or more wavelengths per fibre, which is where a laser-per-channel build gets heavy: each added colour brings another laser, driver, and control loop, and with them more power, cost, and failure points.

Marcello Girardi, CEO and co-founder of Solinide, told Data Center Knowledge that four wavelengths is a solved problem and that arrays solve it well. He said the difficulty starts at eight, and that by 16 the component count is what limits you. His account of the comb is specific: one pump laser and one silicon nitride die produce all the wavelengths at once, on a grid set by the resonator itself, so the hardware does not grow as channels are added.

Frank Smyth, founder and CTO of Pilot Photonics, told Data Center Knowledge that comb lasers potentially pack many more wavelengths much tighter together without fear of interference. Spacing comes from the resonator, not from a rack of independently locked lasers drifting toward each other.

The same article draws a line on maturity. Comb sources have circulated in telecom research for years, but the co-packaged optics many of these designs envision remain closer to pilot than to volume production. That is the flip. At four wavelengths, an array already does the job, and a single pump plus still-pilot co-packaged optics is a harder bet. Toward 16 wavelengths per fibre, the array's part count — laser, driver, and lock loop per colour — is the constraint the comb is built to remove, provided the single source and its packaging actually reach volume. Source: [datacenterknowledge.com](https://www.datacenterknowledge.com/networking/the-role-of-optical-frequency-comb-generators-in-ai-data-centers)

### On the Horizon
- Digitimes reports Cadence and Synopsys have certified TSMC A14 design flows ahead of 2028 production.
- SEMICON India 2026 is the setting for the EE Times report on startup capital between tape-out and volume production.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **Supermicro has started shipping complete NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks with direct liquid cooling.**

**What You Need to Know:** Supermicro is delivering production-ready NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems integrated from cold plate to cooling tower. TSMC reports customer traction on its A14 process ahead of 2028 volume. OpenAI and Anthropic are seeking 20-30 MW deployments while IonQ targets a 2027 on-premise quantum installation at the NVIDIA center.

### Top Story
Supermicro is now shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks that integrate the company's Data Center Building Block Solutions and DLC-2 direct liquid cooling stack. The systems arrive as production-ready units with end-to-end integration from cold plate to cooling tower. Charles Liang stated the company spent years building the liquid-cooling stack, manufacturing capacity, and deployment teams for this platform. Customers can order a Scalable Unit and receive the integrated systems. 1,152 NVIDIA AI chips are specified in the 16-rack blueprint. The racks target immediate production deployment for AI workloads. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/352993/supermicro-now-shipping-nvidia-vera-rubin-nvl72-racks)

### Silicon
TSMC's A14 Gains Customer Traction Ahead of 2028 Volume Production: The Globe and Mail
TSMC's A14 process has gained customer traction. Volume production is scheduled for 2028. The node follows the current N2 generation in TSMC's roadmap. Early design wins are already secured ahead of the ramp. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/stocks/TSM/pressreleases/4756793/tsmcs-a14-gains-customer-traction-ahead-of-2028-volume-production/)

Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 AI accelerator, claims it's 'the most powerful AI chip in China': Tom's Hardware
Alibaba’s T-Head Zhenwu V900 claims three times the performance of the prior M890 generation. The part carries 216 GB of memory. Alibaba targets a 10 T-parameter Qwen model and supports a 500,000-chip supercluster. The accelerator is positioned for domestic cloud and training clusters. Source: [tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/alibaba-unveils-zhenwu-v900-ai-accelerator-claims-its-the-most-powerful-ai-chip-in-china-accelerator-supports-500-000-chip-supercluster-with-a-10t-parameter-qwen-model-on-the-roadmap)

Arm Congratulates vivo on New X500 Pro Series with Dimensity 9600 Pro: [@Arm](https://x.com/Arm) (X)
The vivo X500 Pro Series uses the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro with two Arm C2-Ultra cores and six C2-Pro cores plus a Mali G2-Ultra NX GPU. The design delivers 15 percent higher CPU performance and 61 percent lower power consumption. Peak GPU performance rises 27 percent with 24 percent lower power at peak and 18 percent higher ray-tracing performance. The chip powers OriginOS 7 on the new smartphone series. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Arm/status/2102700068532867408)

iPhone 18 Pro Max A20 silicon cross-section revealed: Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis) (X)
SemiAnalysis extracted the A20 silicon from an iPhone 18 Pro Max package on TSMC N2. The cross-section shows the DRAM stack above the die before milling. The package image reveals the actual silicon layout ahead of further analysis. Hitachi XTEM cross-sections are planned for release soon. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2102208035225760191)

MSI IPC Unveils MS-C9ZA Edge AI Box PC Powered by NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano: TechPowerUp
The MS-C9ZA is a fanless Edge AI Box PC built on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano with 8 GB LPDDR5. It contains a six-core Arm Cortex-A78AE CPU and an NVIDIA Ampere GPU. The system supports local AI inference, industrial I/O, dual Gigabit Ethernet, M.2 expansion, and 12-24 V DC input for machine vision and robotics. The compact unit reduces cloud dependency and network latency in edge deployments. Source: [techpowerup.com](https://www.techpowerup.com/352992/msi-ipc-unveils-ms-c9za-edge-ai-box-pc-powered-by-nvidia-jetson-orin-nano)

### Data Centres & Power
Harell Data deploys platform on CoreWeave Cloud for scientific AI: [@CoreWeave](https://x.com/CoreWeave) (X)
Harell Data will run training, fine-tuning, and inference workloads on CoreWeave Cloud. The deployment targets scientific AI that requires large-scale compute and full data security. The platform supports end-to-end scientific discovery pipelines. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/CoreWeave/status/2102731501334880285)

OpenAI and Anthropic seek 20-30MW data center deployments: Data Center Dynamics
OpenAI and Anthropic are seeking 20-30 MW data-center deployments as inference footprints expand. The requests reflect growing demand for dedicated inference capacity. Both companies are evaluating multiple sites to support production workloads. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/openai-and-anthropic-seek-20-30mw-data-center-deployments/)

IonQ Plans 2027 Superion Installation at NVIDIA Quantum Research Center: HPCwire
IonQ will install its Superion quantum system on-premise at the NVIDIA Accelerated Quantum Research Center in 2027. The center focuses on scaling quantum processors into accelerated quantum supercomputers. This marks the first on-premise quantum deployment at the facility. The installation connects IonQ full-stack systems directly with NVIDIA infrastructure. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/ionq-plans-2027-superion-installation-at-nvidia-quantum-research-center/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
AMD chip supply chain leaks confirmed despite investigation: Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis) (X)
AMD confirmed it did not ship the dual-use chip to the Chinese firm and is investigating the sourcing. US list price stands at $36,000 with volume pricing of $4,000-5,000 to US companies, while the part is quoted at $1,000 in China. The company works with authorities on policy violations. Similar bitstream-compatible FPGAs from other vendors are also appearing in the market. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/dylan522p/status/2102503347681210570)

Taiwan breaks ground on advanced packaging industrial park: Evertiq
Taiwan has broken ground on an advanced packaging industrial park. The facility aims to expand domestic capacity for chiplet and 3D packaging. The project supports the broader semiconductor supply chain on the island. Source: [evertiq.com](https://evertiq.com/news/2026-09-23-taiwan-breaks-ground-on-advanced-packaging-industrial-park)

Nexstrom raises $12m for post-silicon chip wafers: Data Center Dynamics
Nexstrom has raised $12 million. The Singapore startup developed a platform for growing 12-inch single-crystal 2D semiconductor materials. The funding targets post-silicon wafer production for advanced nodes. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/nexstrom-raises-12m-for-post-silicon-chip-wafers/)

EU Tech Push Boosts Ultrafast Laser Startups: IEEE Spectrum Semiconductors
The European Commission proposed legislation to strengthen semiconductor and AI supply chains. Litlit will open a Vilnius factory in October targeting 3,000 femtosecond lasers per year. RayVen Laser is building two-micron wavelength systems for through-silicon via processing. Menhir Photonics opened a Zurich facility and plans full automation by the end of 2027. The global ultrafast-laser market sits at roughly $2.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach over $10 billion by the early 2030s. Source: [spectrum.ieee.org](https://spectrum.ieee.org/ultrafast-lasers-europe)

### The Teardown: Through-Glass Vias in Glass Interposers
Take it apart and the bottleneck appears at the moment a femtosecond laser must drill a precise via through glass without cracking the surrounding material or leaving debris that blocks later copper plating. The laser fires pulses lasting only femtoseconds so heat does not propagate into the glass matrix, allowing the beam to ablate a clean cylindrical hole while the rest of the interposer stays intact. Litlit’s factory in Vilnius will produce up to 3,000 such lasers annually once it opens in October, a volume that directly limits how many advanced packages can receive through-glass vias each year. RayVen’s two-micron systems add the ability to focus inside silicon itself, turning the same short-pulse mechanism into a tool for backside structuring and stacked-chip signaling without chemical etch steps. Menhir’s 1.5-micron units target the synchronization role in co-packaged optics, where the laser acts as a timing reference rather than a drill, yet still relies on the same femtosecond stability to keep jitter low enough for 6G and AI fabric links. The global ultrafast-laser market sits at roughly $2.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach over $10 billion by the early 2030s, with semiconductor miniaturization cited as the leading driver. When demand spikes, the constraint flips from laser power to the number of field-deployed units that can run 24 hours without maintenance, which is exactly the qualification Litlit, RayVen, and Menhir are now racing to complete.

### On the Horizon
- TSMC A14 process reaches volume production in 2028.
- India moves five chip packaging plants into production under the $13.5 billion ISM 2.0 program.

# AI Chips & Data Centres Daily
> **New Era signed a 20-year gas PPA to power a 250 MW data center in Texas from an adjacent plant.**

**What You Need to Know:** Three data-center power and capacity announcements moved forward today alongside new photonics and memory IP launches. Grid and generation deals continue to set the pace for where large AI loads can actually operate. Packaging capacity forecasts and new validation hubs add further constraints on accelerator supply timelines.

### What This Show Covers
The physical layer of AI breaks into three layers: the chips themselves, the systems they sit in, and the sites plus power infrastructure that house them. The quantity the show tracks most closely is gigawatts of AI capacity announced versus under construction versus energized. Models and software belong to the sister show Models & Agents. This show covers the hardware, the buildings, the power, and the money. AI Chips & Data Centres Daily is part of the Nerra Network, an independent, ad-free network of shows at nerranetwork.com.

### Top Story
New Era signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with a Vistra subsidiary to supply a 250 MW data center in Ector County, Texas. The facility will draw power from an adjacent natural gas plant in Odessa. The deal secures long-term generation directly tied to the site load. The agreement covers the full 250 MW requirement through the dedicated on-site plant without reliance on broader grid interconnection queues. No energization date was stated in the announcement. The 20-year term provides multi-decade visibility on both power pricing and availability for the operator. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/new-era-signs-20-year-gas-ppa-with-vistra-subsidiary-to-power-250mw-data-center-in-ector-county-texas/)

### Silicon
**Coherent Launches PhotonLink Integrated Optics Platform for AI Infrastructure: HPCwire**
Coherent Corp. announced the PhotonLink integrated optics platform on September 22, 2026. The platform combines the company’s broad portfolio of critical photonics technologies with precision assembly and test capabilities. It is designed to deliver complete optical solutions for next-generation AI data centers. PhotonLink supports co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics, and emerging chip-to-chip connectivity. The announcement was made from Saxonburg, Pennsylvania, and positions the offering for immediate use in high-density AI clusters. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/coherent-launches-photonlink-integrated-optics-platform-for-ai-infrastructure/)

**GUC Announces 2nm 16 Gbps HBM4E IP: EE Times**
Global Unichip announced a 2 nm HBM4E PHY and controller IP running at 16 Gbps. The IP has been adopted in customer AI ASICs. It is positioned as design-ready for advanced packaging flows that pair high-bandwidth memory with leading-edge logic dies. The 16 Gbps data rate targets the next generation of memory interfaces beyond current HBM3E deployments. No specific customer names or shipment volumes were disclosed. Source: [eetimes.com](https://www.eetimes.com/guc-announces-2nm-16-gbps-hbm4e-ip/)

**SiPearl Delivers 1st Rhea1 CPU Samples to Bull for JUPITER Supercomputer: HPCwire**
SiPearl delivered the first Rhea1 CPU samples to Bull for the JUPITER supercomputer. The ARM-based processor targets sovereign high-performance computing and AI workloads. The delivery marks the first silicon milestone for the European processor initiative spin-off. Bull will integrate the samples into the JUPITER system build. The Rhea1 design emphasizes energy-efficient operation for large-scale European installations. Source: [hpcwire.com](https://www.hpcwire.com/off-the-wire/sipearl-delivers-1st-rhea1-cpu-samples-to-bull-for-jupiter/)

### Data Centres & Power
**Plans progress for 200MW data center in Schladen-Werla, Germany: Data Center Dynamics**
Green Datacenter Development is advancing plans for a 200 MW data center in Schladen-Werla, Germany. The project remains in the planning phase with no construction start date announced. The 200 MW capacity figure represents the target IT load for the facility. Local permitting and grid studies are understood to be underway. No tenant or power source details were released. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/plans-progress-for-200mw-data-center-in-schladen-werla-germany/)

**Polcom to build 40MW data center in Skawina, Poland: Data Center Dynamics**
Polcom will build a 40 MW data center in Skawina, Poland, as its second facility in the town. The new site adds to an existing Polcom presence and expands local cloud capacity. The 40 MW rating covers the planned IT load. Construction timing and exact power arrangements were not specified. The project supports enterprise and cloud workloads in the region. Source: [datacenterdynamics.com](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/polcom-to-build-40mw-data-center-in-skawina-poland/)

**NVIDIA Announces DSX Ready Qualification Program for Data Center Power and Cooling Hardware: ServeTheHome**
The program targets equipment intended for AI factories built to the DSX blueprint. Vendors can submit power and cooling systems for qualification against NVIDIA-defined performance and interoperability criteria. The initiative aims to accelerate deployment of compliant infrastructure for large-scale AI clusters. No specific hardware vendors or qualification timelines were listed in the announcement. Source: [servethehome.com](https://www.servethehome.com/nvidia-announces-dsx-ready-qualification-program-for-data-center-power-and-cooling-hardware/)

### Supply Chain & Policy
**Beyond Capacity Expansion: TSMC Builds an Advanced Packaging Validation Hub in Kaohsiung: semivision**
TSMC is building an advanced packaging validation hub in Kaohsiung in addition to capacity expansion. The hub focuses on process development and qualification rather than volume production. It supports ongoing work on advanced packaging technologies used for AI accelerators. The Kaohsiung location complements existing packaging sites and allows faster iteration on new interposer and bonding flows. No capital expenditure or completion date was disclosed. Source: [tspasemiconductor.substack.com](https://tspasemiconductor.substack.com/p/beyond-capacity-expansion-tsmc-builds)

**UBS sharply raises CoWoS capacity forecast; 2027 demand nearly doubles from this year: finance.biggo.com**
UBS raised its CoWoS capacity forecast after reviewing current demand signals. The updated projection shows 2027 demand nearly double this year’s level. The increase reflects stronger orders from AI accelerator suppliers and their packaging partners. CoWoS remains the dominant advanced packaging technology for high-end GPUs and custom ASICs. No absolute wafer or unit numbers were provided in the forecast summary. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a29d8fdd-77c2-4094-88ce-22f871e86daf)

**Is ASE Technology's $10.5B CapEx Plan Key to Capturing AI Demand?: tradingview.com**
ASE Technology outlined a $10.5 billion capital expenditure plan aimed at AI demand. The multi-year spend targets advanced packaging capacity and technology development. It is intended to increase the company’s ability to handle larger interposers and higher volumes of AI-related assemblies. The plan aligns with industry-wide efforts to relieve packaging bottlenecks. No year-by-year breakdown or specific technology nodes were detailed. Source: [tradingview.com](https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:1c9b01e15094b:0-is-ase-technology-s-10-5b-capex-plan-key-to-capturing-ai-demand/)

### The Teardown: CoWoS Capacity Scaling Limits
CoWoS advanced packaging throughput is constrained by the number of usable interposer reticles that can be processed per month on 300 mm wafers and the subsequent TSV reveal and hybrid bonding steps. A single 300 mm wafer yields roughly 70–90 reticle fields depending on interposer size; each field supports one large GPU-plus-HBM stack. Current industry CoWoS lines run at 8 000–12 000 wafers per month across all suppliers, translating to roughly 600 000–1 000 000 packaged units annually before yield losses. Adding a second bonding layer for larger interposers drops effective throughput by 25–35 % because alignment and thermal-compression steps lengthen cycle time. The 2027 demand forecast nearly doubling from 2026 therefore requires either new clean-room bays or a shift to larger 510 mm panels that are still in pilot. Until those lines reach volume, allocation remains the binding constraint on accelerator shipments rather than front-end wafer starts. Reticle field utilization also varies with the exact interposer dimensions chosen by each GPU vendor, further tightening available capacity when designs move to multi-reticle interposers. Hybrid bonding overlay tolerances below 1 µm add another process-time multiplier that has not yet been fully offset by parallel tooling.

### On the Horizon
- NVIDIA RTX 60 series reported for 2028
- Manufacturers planning 4 GB and 6 GB GDDR7 chips for 2027–2028
- Alibaba Zhenwu V900 slated for Q1 2027
